q1_issues.issue: The purpose head To is used for a result infinitive ("dropped ... to close at 8,120.24"): the index did not drop in order to close, yet the seeded purpose bridge will read this as the drop's purpose.
The scale symbol magnitude is not a surface dimension of the sentence — no gradable adjective and no dimension noun is stated for the drop, so the scale is invented rather than read off the words.
"or 1.3 percent" restates the same drop in other terms, but is emitted as a second independent Measure on the same magnitude scale, so the KB holds two apparently distinct measurements of one event.
Likewise the close is measured on an invented value scale, and the unit point is supplied although "8,120.24" states no unit.

q2_gaps: appositive/equivalence "or" ("107.08 points, or 1.3 percent") — Disjunction treats every "or" as inclusive-disjunctive, with no form for a restatement of the same value
result/outcome infinitive ("dropped ... to close at X") — only purpose infinitives are given the To head, and no head records a non-purposive outcome
a bare numeric change with no stated dimension ("dropped 107.08 points") — Measures requires a stated adjective or dimension noun for the scale slot
a percentage change expressed as a measure — the percent figure is relative to a prior value, which the Measure form has no slot for
notes: Tense, the Weekday time term, the non-volitional-fall Patient on the intransitive subject, and the tenseless embedded close event are all correct.
